scope.purpose: Estimate subscription, AWS storage, compute, transfer, query, logging, and reserve costs before source selection or broad backfill.

observed_facts: Linux/X86 US East (N. Virginia) CPU cost is 0.000011244 USD per vCPU second.
Linux/X86 US East (N. Virginia) memory cost is 0.000001235 USD per GB second.
Additional ephemeral storage cost is 0.0000000308 USD per GB second after the default 20 GB.
Fargate charges from image download start until task or pod termination with one-minute minimum for Linux containers.
AWS Batch has no additional service charge; jobs pay for underlying AWS resources such as EC2, Lambda, or Fargate.
Perpetuals Professional is listed at 900 USD per month.
Professional access includes raw data replay API and Tardis Machine replay APIs per Tardis billing documentation.
Free Trial is listed at 0 USD with 5 file downloads total.
Plus is listed at 79 USD per month with unlimited downloads, Polymarket plus Binance data, daily updates, and personal-use license.
Enterprise is custom priced with commercial-use license.
Archive page states free hourly snapshots of Polymarket, Kalshi, Limitless, and Opinion orderbook data in Parquet format.
Archive page states CC BY 4.0 license with commercial use allowed with attribution.
Current Polymarket v2 index page listed hourly parquet objects from 380.4 MB to 591.4 MB in the parsed sample.
Binance Data Collection offers public market data in daily and monthly files.
The README documents checksum sidecars for archive file integrity.
Durable storage and derived-use terms remain a source-proof gate before selection.
Kalshi documents historical endpoints for markets, candlesticks, trades, fills, and orders.
No paid historical data subscription price was found on the checked documentation page.
Durable API terms, account limits, and storage rights remain source-proof gates before selection.
Hyperliquid official archive uses requester-pays S3 access.
Docs state uploads happen approximately once a month, no timely-update guarantee, and data may be missing.
Transfer and completeness remain source-proof gates before selection.

scenario_estimates.basis: Parsed current PMXT Polymarket v2 index HTML only; not accepted coverage proof.
scenario_estimates.slow_backfill_risk: A broad one-year PMXT Polymarket v2 download is multi-terabyte before conversion, catalog writes, and validation scans.

scenario_estimates.basis: Portable compute baseline, not final worker selection.
Portable compute baseline for heavier replay/conversion pass, not final worker selection.
Combines PMXT index extrapolation, S3 Standard storage, one Athena full scan, and one 100h Fargate backfill worker. Excludes provider fee and dashboard product cost.

backfill_efficiency_controls: Build source coverage ledgers from indexes/manifests before downloading large raw objects.
Choose bounded tranches by source binding, table family, date window, instrument universe, object count, and byte budget.
Require checksum/hash sidecars or staged object hashes before conversion.
Convert only accepted source-proof tranches into NT catalog data.
Run catalog read-back and source-proof/result-contract checks on the bounded tranche before expanding.
Do not use venue names as production-code branches; venue/provider-specific behavior belongs in config-owned source bindings and adapter registry entries.

Throughput benchmark for raw download, conversion, catalog write, and catalog read-back.
Durable license/terms evidence for each accepted source.
Dashboard/read-model product cost, if selected later.
Whether final compute should be Fargate, EC2/Batch, local, or another AWS service after benchmarking.
